message.content:
Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows bilateral, patchy, migratory-appearing peripheral consolidations (often described as "reverse bat-wing" or subpleural opacities), which is the classic radiographic presentation of Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP). The clinical history of a subacute illness (2 months) with fever unresponsive to antibiotics further supports this diagnosis over bacterial pneumonia or tuberculosis.
